ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ inscribed in circle $\odot O$ has a side length of $2\sqrt{3}$ cm. What is the area of this regular hexagon in cm$^{2}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct \(OH \perp AB\) at point H, and connect OA and OB.\\
Since the side length of the inscribed regular hexagon ABCDEF in circle \(O\) is \(2\sqrt{3}\) cm,\\
Therefore, OA = OB = AB = \(2\sqrt{3}\) cm,\\
Therefore, OH = OA\(\cdot\cos 30^\circ\) = \(2\sqrt{3} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) = 3 (cm),\\
Therefore, the area of the regular hexagon ABCDEF = 6\(\cdot\) Area of \(\triangle OAB\) = 6\(\cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2\sqrt{3}\cdot 3\) = \(\boxed{18\sqrt{3}}\) (cm)\(^{2}\).

Let the side length be s = 2√3 from the text. Decompose the hexagon visually into a central rectangle between the vertical lines through A,C and F,D plus two congruent side triangles ABC and FED.
